text:
maria: Heads up — hitting a nasty ordering/parity issue in the sampleapp when using the embeddings+rerank flow under load. Node SDK + batching helper sometimes returns embeddings that don’t line up with the candidate IDs. Repro is fairly consistent on our dev cluster.

jamal: Can you paste the minimal repro? which SDK version? and what do you mean by "don’t line up" — are vectors missing or swapped?

maria: Using node-sdk v0.7.2. Example: we send a batch of candidates like:
```json
{
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "foo"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "bar"},
    {"id": "c3", "text": "baz"}
  ]
}
```
Server-side rerank expects embeddings returned in the same order as candidates, but sometimes the SDK batching helper retries an auth-failure and the final embeddings array is a different ordering or has placeholders removed — so mapping by index (0->c1) yields wrong pairs.

elaine: do you have logs? pattern sounds like retry + merge code dropping placeholders.

maria: yes, logs show the helper doing a retry on 401 then reassembling batches. snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T15:02:13Z] batcher: send batch id=bb7 seq=1 size=3
[2026-03-18T15:02:13Z] server: 401 unauthorized (token rotated) trace=tr-9a1
[2026-03-18T15:02:13Z] batcher: retrying batch id=bb7 seq=1 with backfill placeholders
[2026-03-18T15:02:14Z] batcher: got partial response size=2 (dropped 1 placeholder)
[2026-03-18T15:02:14Z] batcher: merge result -> final array length=3 but order shuffled
```

sam: Oof. That partial response/dropped placeholder is the smoking gun. We do a naive splice/concat on merge which doesn't re-insert original indices when responses are partial.

toni: Is this only Node? Python SDK uses the same batching helper concept but different merge logic. Might explain parity issues.

maria: Python seems fine in our quick tests. Node's helper code path tries to reduce memory by trimming placeholder nulls when response length < request length, then concatenates chunks assuming positional stability. Under retry the chunk order can change (race) and we lost explicit IDs.

jamal: Short term workaround: map by id on the server side (have embeddings include the candidate id in the response) or pass a unique input_id with each candidate and insist the API echoes it back. Do we currently send any per-input id?

maria: No — current embeddings response is just an array of vectors. No ids. That's the root cause: index-only mapping + client-side merge fragility.

elaine: We should not rely on implicit ordering for production APIs. Proposal: require embedding responses to include an explicit `input_id` field or return an array of {id, embedding} objects. That also helps SDK parity across languages.

jamal: Agreed. That’s an API-level change (breaking) — but we can do a non-breaking augmentation: add optional `input_ids` in response and a server flag `preserve_order:true` for compatibility. Then SDKs can switch to using the echoed ids when present.

toni: For immediate mitigation in Node sampleapp: patch the batching helper to attach a per-input uuid and preserve a mapping table before sending; on merge, always reindex using those uuids instead of relying on array order. That’s low-risk and can be backported.

sam: I pushed a quick patch to the sampleapp that maps by `client_input_id` if present. Example change:
```js
// before: assume idx order
const result = response.embeddings.map((e, i) => ({ id: candidates[i].id, vec: e }));
// after: map by echoed id when available
const idMap = new Map(response.embeddings.map(e => [e.client_input_id || generateFallback(), e]));
const result = candidates.map(c => ({ id: c.id, vec: idMap.get(c.client_input_id) }));
```

maria: Thanks — that helps for the sampleapp. But we should also fix the SDK helper to be idempotent-safe. Jamal, can you open an SDK GH issue and label for backport?

jamal: On it. I'll open: "node-batcher: preserve per-input ids and robust merge on partial responses". I'll tag @elaine for runtime changes and @maria for sampleapp test.

elaine: From runtime side we can also add a short-term header `X-Preserve-Order: true` that causes the server to respond with `client_input_id` echoed in each embedding result. That buys us time before a formal API change. ops-bot pls note for deploy consideration.

ops-bot: Noted. deploy window required if header handling added. Recommend staging test first.

toni: Tests: add a fuzz test that simulates partial responses + out-of-order roundtrips for the batcher and assert mapping by client_input_id yields correct pairing. I'll add that to the Node SDK test suite.

sam: Workarounds for customers: 1) pin SDK to python for critical pipelines, 2) disable SDK auto-retries (set retry: 0) until patch, 3) small sampleapp patch (PR done) that maps by id if included.

maria: Action items: jamal - GH issue + label, elaine - header + staging change, toni - unit/e2e tests in node-sdk, sam - merge sampleapp patch, maria - add an integration test to the retriever. I'll follow up with a short RFC on API augmentation (echoing input ids). :eyes: :+1:

jamal: Thanks. I'll post the issue link here after creating.

sam: merged sampleapp fix to branch `hotfix/embed-id-map` — rolling to dev now.

maria: Verified on dev: with hotfix, no more misaligned pairs during a 10k request soak. Great catch, team. :tada:
